column1: Which Python visualization library offers comprehensive, highly customizable static, animated or interactive plots but is complicated to use?
column2: Matplotlib.

column1: What does pandas plotting use behind the scenes, and what is it good for?
column2: Matplotlib; it is good for quick checks but cannot do sophisticated, pretty-looking plots.

column1: What is Seaborn built on, and which data structures is it closely integrated with?
column2: It is built on top of Matplotlib and integrated closely with pandas data structures.

column1: Which library does the lecture name as more popular for interactive visualizations and dashboards?
column2: Plotly.

column1: What does Seaborn provide on top of Matplotlib?
column2: A high-level interface for drawing attractive and informative statistical graphics.

column1: What does a Seaborn axes-level function plot onto, and what does it return?
column2: A single Matplotlib `Axes` object, which is also its return value.

column1: What does a Seaborn figure-level function return?
column2: A Seaborn object, usually a `FacetGrid`, that manages the whole figure.

column1: How do you set the axis labels on the result of `sns.displot()`?
column2: `displot()` returns a figure-level `FacetGrid`, so use `g.set_axis_labels("Temperature", "counts")`.

column1: How do you set the axis labels on the result of `sns.histplot()`?
column2: `histplot()` returns an axes-level `Axes`, so use `ax.set_xlabel(...)` and `ax.set_ylabel(...)`.

column1: Which Seaborn function plots the distribution of one numerical feature as a histogram, KDE or ECDF?
column2: `displot()`, choosing the plot with `kind` (histogram is the default).

column1: What does a KDE plot (`kind='kde'`) show?
column2: The estimated probability density of a continuous variable as a smooth curve, a less cluttered alternative to a histogram.

column1: What does an ECDF plot (`kind='ecdf'`) show?
column2: For each value, the proportion of data points that fall at or below it (the empirical cumulative distribution).

column1: Which two parameters set the size of a Seaborn figure-level plot?
column2: `height` and `aspect`; there is no `width` parameter.

column1: How is the width of a Seaborn figure-level plot determined?
column2: width = `aspect` × `height`; `aspect` defaults to 1.0.

column1: What width does `sns.displot(..., height=3, aspect=2)` produce?
column2: 6 (twice the height of 3).

column1: Which parameter changes the colour of the marks in a Seaborn plot?
column2: `color`, e.g. `color='green'`.

column1: How do you switch Seaborn to a white background with grid lines?
column2: `sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")`.

column1: Name the other built-in Seaborn styles besides `whitegrid`.
column2: `darkgrid`, `ticks`, `dark` and `white`.

column1: What does calling `sns.set_theme()` with no arguments do?
column2: It switches from Matplotlib's current default look to Seaborn's default theme and style, which has the grid on.

column1: Which Seaborn call draws a scatter plot of two numerical features?
column2: `sns.relplot(data=df, x=..., y=..., kind='scatter')`.

column1: How do you add a categorical feature to a scatter plot as colour?
column2: Pass it as `hue`, e.g. `hue='TEMP_category'`.

column1: How did the lecture turn quarters 1–4 into category names before using them as `hue`?
column2: `df['quarter'].map({1:'one', 2:'two', 3:'three', 4:'four'})`.

column1: Which Seaborn function is the interface for categorical plots, and how is the plot type chosen?
column2: `catplot()`; its `kind` parameter selects the underlying axes-level function.

column1: Which `catplot()` kind plots the counts of one categorical feature?
column2: `kind='count'` (`countplot()`).

column1: What do the categorical estimate plots `kind='point'` and `kind='bar'` show?
column2: An estimate (the mean by default) of the numerical feature for each category, with confidence intervals.

column1: What is the default `kind` of `catplot()`?
column2: `'strip'`.

column1: Strip plot vs swarm plot: what is the difference?
column2: Both show every data point per category; a strip plot lets points overlap, a swarm plot places them so they do not overlap.

column1: What does a box plot (`kind='box'`) show?
column2: The minimum, Q1, median, Q3 and maximum, with outliers drawn as separate points.

column1: What does a violin plot (`kind='violin'`) show that a box plot does not?
column2: The shape of the distribution as a curve for each category.

column1: What extra detail does a boxen plot (`kind='boxen'`) give over a box plot?
column2: More boxes at further percentiles (e.g. 25%, 50%, 75%, 95%), which describe the tails of the distribution.

column1: Which parameter sets the number of boxes in a boxen plot, and what values can it take?
column2: `k_depth`: `'full'` (all possible boxes), `'trustworthy'` (only statistically reliable ones) or an integer.

column1: How do you show a summary statistic of a numerical feature per category with `relplot()`?
column2: Put the category on x, the number on y and set `kind='line'`; each category gets one y value, the mean by default.

column1: How do you make `relplot()` or `catplot()` plot the sum per category instead of the mean?
column2: Pass `estimator=sum`.

column1: How do you split a Seaborn figure into sub-plots by a categorical feature?
column2: Set `col='feature'` for columns and/or `row='another feature'` for rows.

column1: What does `col_wrap=2` do in `sns.displot(..., col='quarter', col_wrap=2)`?
column2: It wraps the column sub-plots so there are at most 2 per row.

column1: How do you give each sub-plot its own x-axis in `displot()`?
column2: Pass `facet_kws={'sharex': False}`.

column1: What does `sns.pairplot()` draw?
column2: Pair-wise scatter plots for every pair of numerical features (it is slow on a large DataFrame, so select columns first).

column1: What does `sns.jointplot()` show?
column2: The relationship between two numerical features together with each feature's marginal distribution.

column1: How do you draw a correlation heatmap of a DataFrame's numerical features?
column2: `sns.heatmap(df.corr(numeric_only=True), cmap='coolwarm')`.

column1: How do you plot two categorical features together with `catplot()`?
column2: Put one on `x` (e.g. `kind='count'`) and the other in `hue` or `col`.

column1: What is Plotly Express, and how is it usually imported?
column2: Plotly's high-level, easy-to-use interface, imported as `import plotly.express as px`.

column1: What does every Plotly Express function return?
column2: A `plotly.graph_objects.Figure` instance, built from graph objects internally.

column1: Why use Plotly Express rather than `plotly.graph_objects` directly?
column2: A figure made in one Plotly Express call could take 5 to 100 times more code with graph objects alone.

column1: In `px.scatter`, which parameters encode extra variables beyond x and y?
column2: `color`, `size` and `symbol`; `hover_name` sets the hover label.

column1: How do you load the gapminder sample dataset in Plotly Express?
column2: `px.data.gapminder()` (others include `px.data.stocks()`).

column1: What does a sunburst chart (`px.sunburst`) show?
column2: Hierarchical data as concentric rings, one ring per level, with slice area encoding a value such as population.

column1: Which Plotly Express function draws a polar bar chart, and which parameters set radius and direction?
column2: `px.bar_polar`, with `r` for the value and `theta` for the direction.

column1: Which two kinds of location information can Plotly use to plot data over a map?
column2: Latitude/longitude pairs, or country codes such as ISO-3 `iso_alpha`.

column1: Which Plotly Express function colours countries by a value?
column2: `px.choropleth`, with `locations` set to the ISO-3 country codes.

column1: How do you animate a Plotly Express chart over time?
column2: Pass `animation_frame`, e.g. `animation_frame='year'`, to a function such as `px.scatter` or `px.scatter_geo`.
